preconditions.expression: all(c in '()' for c in stdin.splitlines()[0]) and all(c in '()' for c in stdin.splitlines()[1])

The lengths of s and t are at most 200 characters each.

postconditions.description: The output is either empty or consists only of '(' and ')'.

postconditions.description: The output contains s as a subsequence, where subsequence_indices is a list of indices in stdout where s's characters appear in order.

postconditions.expression: all(t[i] == stdout[j] for i, j in enumerate(subsequence_indices_t) if t[i] == '(') and all(t[i] == stdout[j] for i, j in enumerate(subsequence_indices_t) if t[i] == ')')
postconditions.description: The output contains t as a subsequence, where subsequence_indices_t is a list of indices in stdout where t's characters appear in order.
The output is a regular bracket sequence, where is_regular_bracket_sequence checks if the sequence is balanced and properly nested.

postconditions.expression: not any(len(candidate) < len(stdout.strip()) and is_regular_bracket_sequence(candidate) and all(s[i] == candidate[j] for i, j in enumerate(subsequence_indices_candidate) if s[i] == '(') and all(s[i] == candidate[j] for i, j in enumerate(subsequence_indices_candidate) if s[i] == ')') and all(t[i] == candidate[j] for i, j in enumerate(subsequence_indices_t_candidate) if t[i] == '(') and all(t[i] == candidate[j] for i, j in enumerate(subsequence_indices_t_candidate) if t[i] == ')') for candidate in possible_candidates)
postconditions.description: The output is the shortest possible regular bracket sequence satisfying Q2, Q3, and Q4, where possible_candidates is the set of all shorter regular bracket sequences containing s and t as subsequences.
